issuer: the Land Transport Department (Jabatan Pengangkutan Darat, JPD) of the Ministry of Transport and Infocommunications
note: Read 2026-10-30. The Road Traffic Act (Cap. 68, Laws of Brunei, revised edition 2007, B.L.R.O. 1/2007, read in the copy the ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Assembly's legal network holds, as the Attorney General's Chambers' own copy wasn't found from here), s 21: a person is disqualified from obtaining a driving licence to drive a motor vehicle if under 18. The Land Transport Department's own Driving Licence page: after passing the driving test a driver applies for a provisional driving licence, valid one year, and the full driving licence is a renewal from the provisional licence after that one-year period, chosen for 1, 3, 5 or 10 years (class 1 and 3; one year only for foreign drivers of commercial and public service vehicles and for those 70 and over). So the full licence is held from 19, 18 and the provisional year added (a reading built from the scheme's stages, as Hong Kong's and Malaysia's). The department's Driving Regulation page gives the yearly licence fee as B$10, and the Road Traffic Regulations (revised edition 2007, read in the copy the WTO's import licensing pages hold), Sixth Schedule, charge $10 for a licence valid one year and $30 for three; held as $10 charged for each year held (perYear) with the one-year term, a holder choosing up to ten years at the rate (the 5 and 10 year terms are the department's page's, later than the 2007 Regulations' one or three). The test ($10) and the provisional licence ($5) aren't held. Later amendments to the Act and the Regulations after 2007 weren't read. The identity card (the smart card) isn't this department's; no exchange list was read (foreign licences from Geneva Convention countries are used for up to a year, then converted, on conditions not held).
